title: Bockstein Braiding Statistics Versus Three-Loop Braiding
abstract: Braiding statistics of $p$- and $q$-dimensional topological excitations is conventionally defined in $p+q+2$ spatial dimensions. We find a novel statistical process $W_N(X,Y)=(Y^{-1}X^{-1})^N(YX)^N$ for two order-$N$ excitations in $p+q+1$ dimensions, detecting the Bockstein response $A\smile β(B)$. This new statistics and fermionic loop statistics exhaust all loop statistics in three dimensions whose fusion rules form an Abelian group $G$, classified by $H^5(B^2G,U(1))$. Surprisingly, conventional three-loop braiding goes beyond this classification, so it must have non-Abelian fusion rules. We suggest viewing three-loop braiding as particle-loop braiding together with exotic fusion rules between loops and point-like defects. We also try to clarify the relationship between statistics and symmetry anomaly.
summary: This theoretical work rigorously compares two types of braiding statistics: Bockstein braiding ($W_N$) and conventional three-loop braiding. The authors show that $W_N$ exhausts all loop statistics arising from Abelian fusion rules, but the more complex three-loop braiding must possess non-Abelian features. This advances the understanding of topological order by providing a precise mathematical distinction between different types of quantum entanglement statistics.
main_problem: The paper compares Bockstein braiding statistics with conventional three-loop braiding for topological excitations to determine if they are mathematically equivalent.
main_result: Conventional three-loop braiding goes beyond the classification of loop statistics derived from Abelian fusion rules, suggesting it requires non-Abelian fusion rules or exotic particle-loop interactions.
method: The authors use algebraic methods involving local cancellation criteria and cohomology theory to define and classify topological braiding processes ($W_N$).
model_or_system: The study analyzes topological excitations in $p$- and $q$-dimensional settings, using lattice models based on $\mathbb{Z}_N^2$ toric-code-type ground states.
key_observables: Braiding phase (a value in U(1)), the Bockstein response $\tilde{\beta}(B)$, and the statistical process $W_N(X,Y)$.
important_parameters: The finite order $N$ of the excitations is crucial for the quantization of the statistics.
main_assumptions: The classification relies on assuming Abelian fusion rules when deriving the cohomology bounds, which is then used to contrast with three-loop braiding.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares ordinary, Bockstein, and three-loop braiding in different dimensions. Figure 2 illustrates the Bockstein braiding process using lattice configurations and spacetime histories.
paper_structure: The paper develops a general framework for classifying topological statistics via an 'Excitation Complex,' applies this to define $W_N$, proves its quantization on a lattice model, and finally contrasts this result with three-loop braiding theory.
why_interesting: While the focus is abstract topology, the rigorous mathematical machinery developed—relating quantum phases to cohomology groups and local cancellation criteria—is highly relevant for understanding topological order in condensed matter systems like fractional quantum Hall states or superconducting qubits.
